sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin

items.q: Match the oral drug class to the mechanism or note in the page columns — 1) Biguanide 2) Sulfonylurea 3) Oral GLP-1 analogue 4) SGLT-2 antagonist … A) Metformin/AMP kinase B) Gliclazide with K+ channel action in the column C) Semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide D) Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin
items.exp: The four page columns are biguanide/metformin, sulfonylurea/gliclazide, oral GLP-1 analogues and SGLT-2 antagonists with the listed examples. (Book p933)

items.q: The metformin column says it acts by increasing ___ kinase.
items.exp: Metformin is annotated as acting by increased AMP kinase. (Book p933)

items.q: What HbA1c-reduction range is written in the metformin column?
items.exp: The metformin column gives good HbA1c reduction of 1–2%. (Book p933)

items.q: Assess the metformin notes: I There is no hypoglycemia risk in the column. II The cardiac line points to no risk.
items.exp: The metformin column says no hypoglycemia risk and shows the cardiac line leading to no risk. (Book p933)

items.q: A patient has the renal function threshold written in the metformin column. Which page instruction applies?
opts: Metformin is contraindicated when GFR is below 30 mL/min
Metformin is increased when GFR is below 30 mL/min
Metformin is replaced by insulin at GFR above 90 mL/min
Metformin is used only when GFR is exactly 30 mL/min
items.exp: The metformin column lists contraindication at GFR <30 mL/min. (Book p933)

items.q: Match the drug column to its distinctive page note — 1) Metformin 2) Gliclazide 3) Oral GLP-1 analogue 4) SGLT-2 antagonist … A) Combats resistance B) Only drug in use, antioxidant and vasodilator C) Used in NASH and protective glycemic/cardio/renal notes D) Blocks NLRP3 inflammasome pathway
items.exp: Those distinctive notes appear in the respective four oral-drug columns. (Book p933)

items.q: What HbA1c-reduction range is written for the oral GLP-1 analogue column?
items.exp: The oral GLP-1 analogue column states HbA1c reduction of 2–5%. (Book p933)

items.q: Assess the SGLT-2 notes: I Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are named. II The column says blockade of the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway blocks atherosclerosis.
items.exp: The SGLT-2 column names dapagliflozin and empagliflozin and draws NLRP3 inflammasome-pathway blockade toward blocked atherosclerosis. (Book p933)

items.q: Which group is listed under indications of insulin therapy?
opts: Hybrid diabetes form, T1DM, GDM, HbA1c ≥9.5%, vascular involvement, ketosis or significant polyuria/polydipsia with weight loss
Only mild weight gain with HbA1c below 5.7%
Only a normal glucose value before meals
items.exp: The insulin-indications list includes hybrid form, T1DM, GDM, HbA1c ≥9.5%, macro/microvascular involvement, ketosis and significant polyuria/polydipsia with weight loss. (Book p933)

items.q: Match the insulin type to its page example — 1) Ultra short 2) Short 3) Intermediate 4) Long/ultralong … A) Lispro and Aspart B) Regular C) NPH D) Glargine, Detemir / Degludec
items.exp: The insulin-type line gives ultra-short lispro/aspart, short regular, intermediate NPH, long glargine/detemir and ultralong degludec. (Book p933)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the names printed in the oral GLP-1 analogue column?
items.exp: Semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide are in the oral GLP-1 analogue column; gliclazide is in the sulfonylurea column. (Book p933)

items.q: The final line on this page says CGM should be done before starting:
items.exp: The CGM line states that continuous blood glucose monitoring should be done before starting insulin therapy. (Book p933)
